system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, ivy.chen ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that archive shortly afterward.
At 13:44 UTC, Edge was launched by ivy.chen with quickshare-drop.net as its URL.

At 13:48 UTC, the proxy recorded an Edge tunnel to quickshare-drop.net attributed to ivy.chen, with 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes and 8,800 server-to-client bytes; Zeek independently recorded approximately the same outbound volume.

The sequence of archiving a client-share directory, opening an unapproved file-sharing destination, and sending about 51 MB outbound strongly supports an attempted data exfiltration finding. The available records do not prove that c.zip was the specific content uploaded.

After the transfer, ivy.chen ran C:\Windows\Temp\KB5034441_update.exe /quiet from Explorer; the process later exited. This is suspicious in context, but the records do not establish its origin or relationship to the transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records a TLS CONNECT tunnel and byte counts, not the encrypted request contents or uploaded filenames. The large outbound transfer is recorded in T049-00159 and T049-00161.
The records show the archive command and archive creation, but do not show the archive's contents or directly connect c.zip to the tunnel transfer (T049-00130, T049-00132, T049-00159).
claims_not_established: That c.zip, or any particular files from the Clients directory, were the content sent through the tunnel.
Whether the transfer completed successfully at the destination or whether the destination retained the data.
Whether ivy.chen was authorized to access or share the directory, or her intent.
The provenance, signature, hash, or behavior of KB5034441_update.exe, and whether it is related to the transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine c.zip and relevant source files, including file metadata and hashes, to determine what was staged.
Obtain endpoint browser/download history and forensic evidence for the quickshare-drop.net session and the temporary executable.
Review proxy or destination-side upload records, if available, to identify uploaded filenames, completion status, and account details.
Confirm with ivy.chen and the relevant data owner whether the archive or external transfer was authorized.
